title: Reducing Intensive-Care-Unit-Acquired Muscle Weakness through blood flow restriction training and electromyostimulation
summary:
Muscle weakness often occurs in critically ill patients after long stays in the intensive care unit (ICU), which is called Intensive Care Unit-Acquired Weakness (ICU-AW). This condition leads to long-term functional problems for patients even after they leave the hospital, causing difficulties in returning to work and impacting their quality of life. The economic burden of ICU-AW is significant. However, there's a lack of specific treatments for this condition.
The present study investigates a novel treatment approach involving blood flow restriction (BFR) training combined with electromyostimulation (EMS). BFR training involves using special cuffs to intermittently restrict blood flow to the muscles, aiming to stimulate metabolic responses that counteract muscle breakdown due to immobility. EMS is used to improve voluntary muscle activation, which is often impaired in ICU patients. The combination of BFR and EMS aims to synergistically address neuromuscular activation limitations and muscle atrophy by inducing metabolic stress and increasing muscle activation. The study seeks to investigate the effectiveness and safety of this combined therapy in ICU patients.

interventions.name: Blood-Flow-Restriction + Electromyostimulation Group (BFR-Application with 100% of the individual limb occlusion pressure)
Blood-Flow-Restriction + Electromyostimulation Group (BFR-Application with 100% of the individual limb occlusion pressure + EMS-Training with individual intensity)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The study includes all patients under intensive care monitoring and therapy with a length of stay >48 hours in the surgical intensive care units of the UKB 

All participating patients have signed the patient consent form for participation in the study and the privacy policy after extensive explanation, clarification and information or were represented by the authorized spouse as part of the spousal proxy after extensive explanation
Exclusion criteria:
Acute or chronic infections of the extremities
Open wounds on the lower extremity
Pregnancy and breastfeeding
